\begin{tablenotes}\footnotesize
\item Per target context, the local model, the pooled model (local plus all same-category foreign training data) and the null pooled model are each retuned on the validation users. In the null pooled model each donor country's training user $\times$ product matrix is randomised with the curveball algorithm (at least five trades per user), which keeps every product's interaction count and every user's activity within that donor but breaks which products co-occur in a user's history; its score is the mean over three independent randomisations. ``Pool $-$ null pool'' is the part of the pooling gain that depends on the foreign co-interaction patterns. CIs: two-way cluster bootstrap over countries and categories, 95\%. Rule fixed in advance: the contribution of co-interaction patterns is \emph{supported} if the 95\% CI of the mean of pool $-$ null pool lies entirely above 0. MostPop is a sanity check (largest absolute difference between pool and null pool: Original: $<10^{-15}$, Variants merged: $<10^{-15}$). Variants merged: product variants merged within each market $\times$ category context. EASE is not fitted on catalogues of more than 4000 products; IN Arts \& Crafts is not a context of the variant-merged data. MostPop: no verdict (sanity check).
\end{tablenotes}
